mechanism_narrative: The recent uptick in WORKPLACES and the flatter TRANSIT decline indicate more weekday trips and commuter spillovers. That should lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as routine after-work and lunch visits recover.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise above its last-4-week mean over the next 28 days while WORKPLACES stays near or above -10 and TRANSIT remains near -20.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL stays elevated while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES stay depressed, people substitute local errands and neighborhood shopping for longer trips. That substitution should push RETAIL_REC upward within two weeks and remain supportive for four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase within 14 days despite RESIDENTIAL staying above 10 and both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remaining below their recent means.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in PARKS signals improved outdoor leisure conditions, which spills into recreational shopping and dining trips. If PARKS remains less negative or turns positive, RETAIL_REC should be higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays flat or declines over the next 28 days even though PARKS rises by at least 3 points from its current level and remains improved for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT falls further from its already weak level, access costs for discretionary trips rise and retail visits decline with a short lag. A new downward crossing in TRANSIT should therefore reduce RETAIL_REC over the next one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 2 points week-on-week from an already sub -20 level
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises within 7 to 14 days after a further TRANSIT drop below -22, indicating the mobility shock did not suppress retail activity.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of rising GROCERY_PHARM with still-weak RETAIL_REC implies households are consolidating necessary errands and avoiding discretionary shopping. If grocery trips keep absorbing trip demand, RETAIL_REC should remain lower over the next two to four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 14 to 28 days while GROCERY_PHARM continues to rise above its current level, showing no crowding-out from essentials trips.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES rebounds while RESIDENTIAL eases from its elevated level, time spent away from home expands and discretionary stopovers become more common. That should raise RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES crosses above -8 while RESIDENTIAL falls below 11
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next 28 days after WORKPLACES rises above -8 and RESIDENTIAL drops below 11 for at least two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A recovery in TRANSIT combined with a rebound in WORKPLACES indicates fewer access frictions and more commuting. In that regime, retail mobility should strengthen quickly because discretionary trips are bundled into work journeys.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by at least 2 points and WORKPLACES rises by at least 1 point within the same week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its current 4-week mean two weeks after simultaneous gains in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS improves while GROCERY_PHARM stays positive, weekend and household outing intensity is broad-based rather than substitutionary. That broadening should continue to support RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines for the next 28 days even though PARKS improves by at least 3 points and GROCERY_PHARM remains above zero.
